req.title: Task update persists
req.statement: The system shall persist PUT changes so subsequent GET requests reflect the update.

doc.reasoning: The test suite is designed to verify that the task update functionality in the FastAPI application correctly persists changes to the database. The suite includes a positive test to confirm successful updates, a negative test to handle non-existent task updates, and a boundary test to ensure updates at the edge of valid input ranges are handled correctly. These tests are crafted to catch common mutation errors such as incorrect status codes, improper handling of non-existent resources, and boundary condition failures.

tests.name: test_update_task_success
preconditions: Task with id 5 exists in the database
actions: Send PUT request to update task with id 5
expected: Task title updated to 'Updated Task Title'
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Update task with id 5
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/5",
    json={"title": "Updated Task Title"}
)

assert response.status_code == 200
assert response.json()["title"] == "Updated Task Title"

tests.name: test_update_task_not_found
preconditions: Task with id 999 does not exist in the database
actions: Send PUT request to update task with id 999
expected: Error message indicating task not found
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Attempt to update non-existent task with id 999
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/999",
    json={"title": "Non-existent Task"}
)

assert response.status_code == 404
assert response.json()["detail"] == "Task with id 999 not found"

tests.name: test_update_task_boundary
preconditions: Task with id 4 exists in the database
actions: Send PUT request to update task with id 4 with maximum title length
expected: Task title updated to maximum length
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Update task with id 4 with maximum title length
max_length_title = "T" * 100
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/4",
    json={"title": max_length_title}
)

assert response.status_code == 200
assert response.json()["title"] == max_length_title
